args.body:
COUNTER-REDLINE COVER NOTE

To: Dahlgren & Pike LLP, counsel to Corvid Analytics LLC
From: Harrow & Vane LLP, counsel to Northgale Systems, Inc.
Re: Northgale Systems, Inc. / Corvid Analytics LLC — Master Services Agreement (Corvid rev B counter-draft, 9 July 2026)
Date: 22 July 2026

We refer to Corvid's rev B counter-draft of the Northgale Systems, Inc. client-form master services agreement (v2 execution-ready base), transmitted on 9 July 2026, which supersedes rev A in its entirety. Northgale has reviewed each tracked change in that operative counter-draft against its 2026 commercial contracting playbook. This cover note accompanies Northgale's counterparty redline responding to each tracked change, stating whether Northgale accepts, counters at an approved playbook fallback, or rejects, and carrying the specific figures Northgale's counter-turn will take.

Unless expressly stated below, all other terms of the client form v2 remain accepted as drafted.

1. Section 2.2 — Renewal Period.
   Corvid proposes: automatic renewal for successive two (2) year renewal periods.
   Northgale position: REJECT. Northgale's playbook establishes one (1) year as the standard renewal period and approves no multi-year renewal fallback; multi-year renewal periods of any length are out of policy and require Chief Legal Officer approval. Northgale's counter-turn will hold automatic renewal at successive one (1) year renewal periods, with non-renewal notice remaining sixty (60) days before the end of the then-current term. [This item is flagged for escalation to the Deal Committee separately.]

2. Section 4.3 — Late Interest Rate.
   Corvid proposes: 1.5% per month on late undisputed amounts.
   Northgale position: REJECT/COUNTER. Northgale's playbook provides that late interest never exceeds 1.0% per month. Northgale's counter-turn will set late undisputed amounts to accrue interest at 1.0% per month (or the maximum lawful rate, whichever is lower).

3. New Section 4.4 — Suspension Right.
   Corvid proposes: Provider may suspend Services if any undisputed invoice remains unpaid fifteen (15) days after its due date, until all past-due amounts are paid in full.
   Northgale position: REJECT. A suspension-of-services right is out of policy in Northgale's playbook unless preceded by at least thirty (30) days' written cure notice, and any suspension right of any kind requires CFO sign-off. Corvid's proposal (suspension fifteen (15) days after due date, with no cure window) is rejected as proposed. Northgale's counter-turn will grant Provider no suspension right for non-payment; if a suspension right is to be discussed at all, it must be preceded by at least thirty (30) days' written cure notice and is subject to CFO approval (escalated separately).

4. Section 7.2 — Termination for Convenience Notice Period.
   Corvid proposes: ninety (90) days' prior written notice.
   Northgale position: COUNTER AT APPROVED FALLBACK. Northgale's playbook standard is thirty (30) days; the approved fallback is up to forty-five (45) days; any notice period above 45 days requires CLO approval. Northgale's counter-turn will set Customer's termination-for-convenience notice at forty-five (45) days' prior written notice.

5. New Section 7.4 — Wind-Down Period.
   Corvid proposes: a wind-down period of sixty (60) days, during which Customer pays the full monthly base service fee for wind-down services plus all committed third-party costs.
   Northgale position: COUNTER AT APPROVED FALLBACK. Northgale's playbook permits a post-termination wind-down only if (i) capped at thirty (30) days and (ii) compensation is limited to documented out-of-pocket costs and non-cancelable third-party commitments; full-fee wind-down compensation is out of policy. Northgale's counter-turn will (i) cap the wind-down period at thirty (30) days, and (ii) limit compensation to documented out-of-pocket costs and non-cancelable third-party commitments, and not the full monthly base service fee.

6. Section 9.1 — Limitation of Liability, Cap Measurement Period.
   Corvid proposes: cap measured at the Fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the first event giving rise to liability.
   Northgale position: COUNTER AT APPROVED FALLBACK. Northgale's playbook standard is a twenty-four (24) month measurement period, with an approved fallback floor of eighteen (18) months; a twelve (12) month measurement period is below the fallback floor and requires CLO approval. Northgale's counter-turn will measure the cap at the Fees paid or payable by Customer in the eighteen (18) months preceding the first event giving rise to liability.

7. Section 9.2 — Carve-Out Treatment.
   Corvid proposes: delete clause (c), subjecting gross negligence and willful misconduct to the Section 9.1 cap.
   Northgale position: REJECT. Northgale's playbook provides that the carve-outs for confidentiality, IP indemnification, and gross negligence/willful misconduct are non-negotiable; deletion of any carve-out requires joint CLO and CFO approval. Northgale's counter-turn will retain clause (c), so the Section 9.1 cap does not apply to (a) breach of Section 6 (Confidentiality), (b) Provider's obligations under Section 8 (IP Indemnification), or (c) a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

8. Section 11.2 — Service-Credit Cap.
   Corvid proposes: aggregate service-credit cap of ten percent (10%) of the monthly base service fee in any calendar month.
   Northgale position: COUNTER AT APPROVED FALLBACK. Northgale's playbook standard is an aggregate monthly credit cap of twenty percent (20%), with an approved fallback floor of fifteen percent (15%); a 10% aggregate credit cap is out of policy. Northgale's counter-turn will set the aggregate service-credit cap at fifteen percent (15%) of the monthly base service fee in any calendar month, retaining the credit mechanics (5% of the monthly base fee per 0.1% uptime shortfall below 99.5% Monthly Uptime, subject to the aggregate cap).

We are available to discuss the above. As noted, the renewal-period change and the other out-of-policy asks identified above (suspension right and any departure below a playbook floor) are being escalated to Northgale's Deal Committee, which meets on 4 August 2026, and will be addressed in a separate escalation memorandum. Please direct substantive questions to the undersigned.

— Daniel Kellner, Harrow & Vane LLP
